limitations: Unreviewed candidate decomposition, not an exhaustive reviewed specification inventory. Every current TOC page is indexed, but rule-by-rule completeness, section-anchor accuracy and all edition notes have not been audited. Page coverage is not semantic completeness.

The live official Reference snapshot is byte-pinned, not release-pinned or commit-pinned. No asserted equivalence to repository-pinned rustc 1.98.1. Resolve source/compiler version mismatch before treating differential results as conformance to a single version.

Scope is stable language for edition 2024 on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. Earlier editions, other targets and nightly-only extensions are outside this denominator until separately inventoried. Stable feature-gate rejection must match the pinned release; do not silently enable nightly or RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP.

Contract modes require native CHECK and BUILD plus execution at workers 1 and 8, debug and release, relevant overflow-check settings and supported panic strategies. This artifact defines needed evidence, not a verified list of implemented compiler flags, artifact modes, panic backends or target features.

core/no_std language items, alloc ownership/allocator behavior and std platform services need authentic pinned library-source and runtime evidence. The Rust Reference is not a standard-library API inventory. Library API/version coverage is a separate denominator, not inferred from special types or preludes.

Cargo manifests, dependency resolution/lockfiles/features, build scripts, proc-macro packaging, native linking, test/doc-test harnesses and unchanged real projects need a separate project/tool inventory. Macro language semantics are included here, but that does not establish sandboxing, packaging or ecosystem compatibility.

ABI/layout obligations require independent target-native interoperability tests. Do not demand stock-private Rust ABI, unspecified field ordering, niche choices, vtable bytes, symbol mangling or optimization internals where no external guarantee exists. Private bootstrap transport is not platform ABI conformance.

Diagnostic evidence requires correct acceptance/rejection category and useful original/expansion source attribution, not byte-identical stock wording unless separately specified. Unsupported-valid, invalid Rust, resource limits, infrastructure failures and wrong-code outcomes remain separate.

Unsafe Rust semantics and aliasing/provenance are not fully formally specified by the Reference. UB programs are not valid output-equivalence oracles, and general unsafe UB is not required to be statically rejected. Safe violations and required const-evaluation errors remain rejection obligations.

Not every obligation admits all four executable evidence classes. Source-index pages are explicitly nonsemantic, and unsafe UB versus invalid safe Rust is distinguished in test_needs. Expected class applicability must be reviewed, not converted to an automatic pass.

Many-to-many existing_requirements links identify related bounded legacy scenarios, not semantic equivalence, coverage saturation, implementation support or a test result. Some language obligations currently have no exact existing requirement and may require new case identities.

Interactions here are selected required axes, not exhaustive Cartesian or higher-order combinations. Generated campaigns, minimization, optimizer soundness and source/graph forgery controls remain separate evidence work.
No source code, shared data, compiler artifacts, builds, tests or commits were modified or produced. Only scratch data generation and static inventory checks were performed.

Legacy requirement IDs not referenced by this language inventory are explicitly outside its language-only mapping: library-buffered-bytes, library-collections, library-option, library-results, project-build-scripts, project-unchanged-programs, tooling-cross-feature, tooling-graph-contract, tooling-persistence, tooling-root-gating, tooling-security, tooling-systematic-campaigns, tooling-workflow-performance. These remain in the existing scope and must be covered by library/project/tool inventories, not removed from total compatibility accounting.
